files.why: Only source file; contains carousel markup, CSS transforms, and JS slide positioning that could cause progressive misalignment

diagnosis.root_cause: The track advances by the rounded step Math.round(1000/3)=333px while each card is 1000/3=333.333px wide, so every advance under-shifts the track by 1/3px and the error accumulates in the persistent offset.
diagnosis.mechanism: Each 600ms tick adds the too-small integer step to offset and applies it as translateX without ever recomputing position from the card index; the 0.333px shortfall per tick is never corrected, so card edges drift linearly away from the viewport snap position (about 2.7px after 8 ticks, growing with further ticks) instead of realigning exactly every 3 cards.
diagnosis.test_spec: Drive the page through at least 8-9 auto-advance ticks and, after each tick, measure the track's computed translateX and/or the viewport-relative getBoundingClientRect().left of the card that should be snapped to the viewport's left edge; assert the absolute alignment error versus the nearest exact multiple of 1000/3 stays near zero (<0.1px) and does not increase with tick count, whereas the buggy page shows error growing by ~0.33px per tick in the under-shift direction.

fix_strategies.name: Use exact fractional step
fix_strategies.approach: At the step definition, stop rounding: set step = containerWidth / n (333.333...px) so the per-tick shift exactly matches the rendered card width, eliminating the per-tick shortfall.

fix_strategies.name: Recompute offset from index instead of accumulating
fix_strategies.approach: Inside the interval callback, replace incremental offset += step with an absolute derivation such as offset = ticks * (containerWidth / n) (or Math.round(ticks * containerWidth / n) for pixel snapping), so any rounding is bounded to <1px total and cannot accumulate over time.

fix_strategies.name: Snap to measured card geometry
fix_strategies.approach: Intervene at the transform application: translate the track to the target card's measured offsetLeft (or card.getBoundingClientRect().width accumulated from the DOM) rather than a computed constant, so the track always aligns to the actual laid-out card edge regardless of fractional widths.
